newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week-Freddie. [corrected 20:05 gmt]
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week-Freddie. [corrected 20:05 gmt]

text.p: The average commitment rate on U.S. 30-year fixed rate mortgages fell slightly in the week ending April 11 to an average 8.15 percent from 8.18 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages dipped to 7.67 percent from 7.70 percent, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
But one-year adjustable rate mortgages rose in the week to 5.91 percent from 5.80 percent, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.05 percent, the 15-year 7.56 percent and the ARM 5.80 percent.
"Long-term interest rates seem to have settled down since the Federal Reserve raised short-term rates a few weeks ago," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"We probably won't see much movement in these figures now until release of the next employment report or the Consumer Price Index," Van Order added.
Last week the Labor Department reported a U.S. March unemployment rate of 5.2 percent and a 175,000 increase in non-farm payrolls.
On Friday the Labor Department will issue March producer prices and next week March consumer prices.

Lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, up from 1.7 percent last week. They charged 1.5 percent (corrects from 1.4 percent) on ARM loans, up from 1.4 percent from last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
